abstract: The goal of this paper is to reduce the input token cost of Omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) at inference time. Omni-LLMs reason jointly over audio, video and text, but the cost of the three streams is highly unbalanced: visual tokens account for the vast majority of the input, and are highly redundant. In this paper, we propose ReMo, a training-free framework that compresses visual tokens by redistributing their information across modalities: a visual token is kept only if its information appears nowhere else. ReMo achieves this in two ways: (i) it aligns audio and video in a shared space via closed-form calibration, and removes visual tokens already explained by the audio or by other visual tokens; and (ii) it replaces object-level visual tokens, identified by a lightweight object detector, with compact text proxies, short descriptions of each object and its location, conveying the same content in far fewer tokens. On Qwen2.5-Omni at two model scales, ReMo removes 54% of the input tokens with comparable accuracy. It performs comparably to the full-token model, reaching 101.2% and 101.4% of its average accuracy over five audio-visual benchmarks.
oneSentenceThesis: 针对 Omni 大模型视觉 Token 占九成以上导致推理代价过高的问题，ReMo 在不训练的情况下用音频对齐删冗余视觉 Token 并用带位置的物体词代理补回语义，在 54% 左右的全序列压缩下保持与全量输入相当的精度，但效果依赖音频视频确有重叠且检测器基本正确。
originalTitle: Out of Sight, Still in Mind: Token Compression for Omni-LLMs
readerTitle: 看不见也能记得：把视觉信息分流到音频和文字的 Token 压缩
